record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Let b(P) be the minimum size of a blocking set Q for a finite point set P in general position, and let b(n) be the minimum of b(P) over all n-point sets with no three points collinear. Prove that b(n)/n tends to infinity as n tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7 Prove that as n -> infinity, b(n) / n -> infinity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the plane in general position, meaning that no three points of P are collinear. A blocking set for P is a finite set Q of points in the plane, disjoint from P, such that for every pair of distinct points p, p' ∈ P, the open line segment pp' contains at least one point of Q. (Equivalently, Q "blocks" all visibilities between points of P.) Define
   b(P) = min{ |Q| : Q is a blocking set for P },
and, for each integer n ≥ 3,
   b(n) = min{ b(P) : P ⊂ ℝ² has |P| = n and no three points of P are collinear }.

It is known that b(n) ≥ n − 1 for all n ≥ 3. Prove (or disprove) that
   b(n) / n → ∞   as n → ∞.
artifact.category_tag: Discrete and combinatorial geometry — blocking/visibility sets
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that b(n)/n → ∞ for blocking sets of n points in general position is attributed to Pór and Wood (2010, "Blocking Visibility for Points in General Position"). Subsequent literature (e.g., surveys on visibility/obstacle problems and follow-up work by Pór–Wood and others) continues to list it as an open problem; the best known general lower bound remains linear in n, while the conjectured upper bound O(n log n) and the lower bound b(n) = ω(n) have not been established. No published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Blocking Visibility for Points in General Position
status_evidence.snippet: Pór and Wood study b(P) and b(n), proving linear bounds and conjecturing super-linear growth.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of whether b(n)/n → ∞ is posed as a conjecture by Pór and Wood, with only linear bounds known.

status_evidence.title: On Visibility and Blockers (Pór, Wood)
status_evidence.snippet: Expository paper discussing conjectures on visibility and blockers, including the question of superlinear growth of b(n).
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent expository work by the same authors lists the superlinear-growth question as still open.

status_evidence.title: Obstacle Numbers (Morin)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style page discussing related visibility/blocker problems and citing Pór–Wood conjectures as open.
status_evidence.claim: Survey resources continue to treat the b(n)/n → ∞ conjecture as unresolved.
